description: contractHash conformance (contract-document.md section 6): contractHash = "sha256:" + lowercase-hex(sha256(canonicalJSON(normalize(document)))), canonicalJSON per RFC 8785 (JCS). Each case gives an input `document` (already reflecting whatever projection the case is about) and the exact `expectedHash` a conformant implementation MUST produce after applying normalize() to it. Values were computed independently with two separate RFC 8785 implementations (the `canonicalize` npm package, v4.0.0; the `rfc8785` PyPI package, v0.1.4) piped through SHA-256 — both agreed exactly on all four values below. `minimal` and `topicScoped` documents already have no example/messageEndpoint/transports/reserved entries to strip, so normalize() is a no-op on them and expectedHash is their direct canonical hash; `decorated` and `withReserved` are NOT already normalized (that is the point of those two cases) and MUST be normalized by the implementation under test before hashing, which is why their expectedHash equals `minimal`'s.

cases.name: example-messageEndpoint-transports-are-stripped-by-normalization
cases.description: Same requests/events/components content as minimal-document, decorated with example payloads, messageEndpoint, and transports. normalize() strips all of that, so this MUST hash identically to minimal-document — proving those three fields do not participate in the contract hash.

cases.name: reserved-entries-are-excluded-by-the-domain-projection
cases.description: Same domain content as minimal-document, plus two reserved requests: one flagged reserved:true (benzene:spec), one detected only by the benzene: prefix rule with no flag at all (benzene:healthcheck, the older-producer case). The whole-service contractHash normalize step removes both entries entirely (contract-document.md section 6.2), so this MUST hash identically to minimal-document.

cases.name: topic-scoped-projection
cases.description: The schema-closure (contract-document.md section 5.3) projection of minimal-document for topic orders:create: requests holds only that one entry, events is empty, and components is narrowed to just what orders:create's request/response reach (CreateOrder, OrderDto) — OrderCreated is excluded because it is reachable only from the order:created EVENT, not from orders:create's request/response. This document is already the topic-scoped projection (an implementation computing it from minimal-document via section 5.3 must arrive at exactly this shape); normalize() is then a no-op on it since it already has no example/messageEndpoint/transports/reserved entries.
